extracted.intended_audience: relatively new journal Editors (also useful for experienced editors)
extracted.subtask_description: Two-module e-learning course for journal editors covering the basics and practical aspects of peer review: models and ethics (module 1) and reviewer selection, fraud detection, report assessment, and editorial decision-making (module 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Different models of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers the basics of the peer review process such as the different models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 discusses different peer review models and innovations in peer review as foundational knowledge for editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovations in peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Awareness of new or evolving peer review approaches and innovations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 includes innovations in peer review as a topic to help editors understand emerging practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding and maintaining confidentiality in the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 highlights confidentiality as a core concept editors must manage when handling manuscripts and reviewer identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and management of conflicts of interest affecting reviewers, authors, or editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 1 covers conflicts of interest so editors can recognise, declare, and mitigate COIs in review and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying and inviting reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Processes and criteria for finding and inviting appropriate reviewers for submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 focuses on practical aspects of identifying suitable reviewers and the invitation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of a good reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes and behaviours that define an effective peer reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 describes the characteristics of a good reviewer to guide selection and assessment of reviewer performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author and submission fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition and handling of fraudulent author behaviour or fraudulent submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 addresses author and submission fraud so editors can detect and respond to falsified or manipulated submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer fraud
rubrics_metrics.description: Detection and management of fraudulent reviewer behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 includes reviewer fraud as a topic, alerting editors to risks such as fake reviewer identities or manipulated reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing reviewer reports received
rubrics_metrics.description: Process for evaluating the content and quality of peer review reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 covers how to assess the reports received from reviewers as part of forming an editorial judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: How a Journal Editor makes a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decision-making process based on submissions, reviewer reports, and other considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 explains how editors combine information (reports, ethics, COIs, fraud indicators) to reach a decision on a manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of good and bad peer review within a journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs and metrics that reflect the quality of peer review at the journal level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module 2 discusses indicators of good and bad peer review to help editors monitor and improve review quality across the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal Editors' Code of Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and expectations associated with the role of Editor-in-Chief as set out in the Code of Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate course on the Code provides an overview of the standards editors should uphold; the Code informs ethical and procedural behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling editorial problems with flowcharts and template letters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of best-practice flowcharts and template correspondence to manage common editorial situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor Resources provide flowcharts and template letters to guide responses to routine and exceptional editorial issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to check for appropriate ethics approval for research involving humans or other regulated activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Ethics resources outline ethics approval expectations that editors should verify for submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent to participate in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure studies involving participants report appropriate informed consent procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Ethics materials advise editors to check that authors have obtained and reported informed consent where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics requirements for animal studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and reporting expectations for research involving animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should confirm animal studies meet ethical requirements and reporting standards described in Research Ethics resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trial registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement that clinical trials are registered in appropriate registries prior to participant enrollment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research Ethics guidance reminds editors to verify trial registration information when assessing clinical trial reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism detection and response
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding different types of plagiarism and how to assess and take action on text overlap detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plagiarism course covers types of plagiarism, practicalities of using Crossref Similarity Check, and steps editors should take when overlap is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Crossref Similarity Check (and IRR/iThenticate service)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Crossref Similarity Check and optional IRR (iThenticate Report & Response) service to analyse similarity reports and receive recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IRR service analyses the Crossref Similarity Report and provides editors with a recommendation for new submissions; plagiarism resources describe tool usage and interpretation.
